verdict.rationale: Jina Reader's docs say users can pass an `x-json-schema` JSON schema or a natural-language `x-instruction` header, and ReaderLM-v2 then extracts specific fields. This is LLM-driven field extraction with no pre-written selectors. The evidence is only a brief vendor-docs claim, and it doesn't show the model choosing fields itself or how well extraction works. missing for 10: evidence that the LLM decides which fields to extract without a user-supplied schema, documentation of the structured output format and its limits, and independent or hands-on corroboration of extraction quality.

support.subject: As an ai-native user, I can have an LLM read a page and decide what structured fields to pull out without pre-written selectors

citations.quote: Use the `x-json-schema` header with a JSON schema definition, or use `x-instruction` header with natural language instructions. Both features work with ReaderLM-v2 to extract specific fields
